newsitem.title: CHILE: Massad renomination unconstitutional - Chile panel.
newsitem.headline: Massad renomination unconstitutional - Chile panel.

text.p: A Chilean Senate committee said President Eduardo Frei's renomination of Carlos Massad to the five-member Central Bank board was unconstitutional because Massad had already been rejected by the full Senate.
The 3-2 ruling, with three rightist senators voting against Massad, was a setback to Massad's chances to joining the board, but would probably not be fatal.
But the vote did indicate that Massad, Frei's former health minister, may have more problems winning approval in a second vote in the full Senate than otherwise thought.
Massad, nominated to replace Central Bank president Roberto Zahler who resigned in June, was first rejected by the full Senate by a razor-thin 21-20 margin on August 27.
Government officials said almost immediately that they would reoffer his nomination because two ruling coalition senators were absent for the vote.
Massad's proponents will need 26 votes in the full Senate to overrule the constitutional panel's vote against the renomination, said Christian Democratic senators Juan Hamilton and Anselmo Sule.
The government nominated Massad to the central bank's five-member board.
But officials said publicly that they intended the board then to elect Massad as president to replace Zahler. The government does not nominate the bank's president per se.
